solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poet program occupies most of exhibit (6)

indicators.note: the program takes up room inside the exhibit
SHOW loses its last letter

blocks.note: SHOW = exhibit, minus its final W
an app is a computer program

explanation.surface: A poet's software sits in a gallery display, taking up nearly all of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Program is the modern software sense, an unexpected neighbour for a poet from the sixth century BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho is one of the most famous poets of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Buffeted small railway wagon (6)

blocks.note: s = small, as on clothing labels
in Britain an open railway goods wagon is a truck

explanation.surface: A little railway wagon is knocked about by the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffeted reads as an adjective describing the wagon, but it is the past tense of a verb: hit, struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: waves or wind that buffet a thing hit it hard.

clue.text: Legal cases succeeded against local press agent (9)

indicators.note: LICIT encloses S, like a case round its contents
PUB is placed up against the rest

blocks.note: your local is your nearest pub

explanation.surface: Lawsuits are won against a regional newspaper's PR person.
explanation.walkthrough: Legal cases looks like a noun phrase about lawsuits; it is LICIT casing S. 'Local' as a noun is British for the neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A publicist handles press and publicity for a client.

clue.text: It’s perfect on top of yoghurt! (5)

definitions.text: It’s perfect on top of yoghurt!

indicators.note: take the top, first letter of yoghurt

blocks.note: to hone is to perfect, as a skill

explanation.surface: A cheerful food writer's verdict: nothing beats a drizzle over yoghurt.
explanation.walkthrough: Perfect looks like an adjective but is the verb HONE. The whole sentence is also the definition: honey is the perfect topping for yoghurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey drizzled over yoghurt is a classic pairing.

clue.text: Dish made with eggs — some sell better without any shells (8)

indicators.note: each word loses its outer letters, as an egg loses its shell

blocks.note: sOMe without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A market trader's tip: eggs sell better once you have taken the shells off.
explanation.walkthrough: The shells are the first and last letters of each of the three words; the egg imagery makes the instruction apt.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is beaten eggs cooked in a pan.

clue.text: Doctor claimed refurbished workspace next to river (7,7)

indicators.note: CLAIMED is done up into a new form

explanation.surface: A doctor says a renovated office by the river is theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor reads as a title in the surface; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical officer is a doctor in charge of health in an organisation or area.

clue.text: Call in large loan agreements, causing reputational damage (9)

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing inside another, so the call sits within the loan agreements

blocks.note: l = large, as on clothing labels
IOUs are written promises to repay
to bell someone is British slang for phoning them

explanation.surface: A bank calls in big loans, and its good name suffers for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Call in reads as the banking phrase for demanding repayment; here Call is BELL and in tells you where it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something libellous damages a person's reputation in writing.

clue.text: Every now and again swim past rocky peak in trunks (5)

indicators.note: take every other letter of swim
to swim past something is to go beyond it, so the swim letters come after the peak

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor
S, I: letters 1 and 3 of swim

explanation.surface: A swimmer in trunks occasionally paddles past a craggy outcrop.
explanation.walkthrough: Trunks are swimwear in the surface but are bodies without limbs in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsi is a plural of torso, the trunk of the body.

clue.text: Invigorate Frenchman upset with non-uniform appearance (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, turn RENE upside down
remove U, which is uniform in the phonetic alphabet

blocks.note: RENE, a French man's name, turned over
GUISE = appearance, with its U taken away

explanation.surface: Pep up a troubled French chap who looks scruffy and out of uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-uniform suggests irregular; it means take out U.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to fill someone with energy and vigour.

clue.text: Note lines accompanying lengthy word for part of the brain (4-4,6)

definitions.note: strictly a function of the brain rather than a physical part of it

indicators.note: MEMO and RY go along with LONG TERM

blocks.note: RY = railway, whose lines are its tracks

explanation.surface: A long technical word noted down as a label for a brain region.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines for RY is a standard crossword shorthand: railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-term memory is the brain's store of lasting memories.

clue.text: Heroic tale of Ohio-born Liberal Democrat (5,4)

definitions.note: Robin Hood is the hero of the tale, and his name is used for the tale itself

indicators.note: take liberties with the letters of OHIO-BORN

blocks.note: d = Democrat, as in US politics

explanation.surface: A political tale about a hero born in Ohio who stood for the Liberal Democrats.
explanation.walkthrough: Liberal Democrat is a UK party name, but Liberal is the anagram signal and only Democrat gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the English outlaw hero of the ballads and tales told about him.

clue.text: Seize westbound drug boat (5)

indicators.note: an across answer reads west to east, so going west runs GRAB right to left

explanation.surface: Customs officers board a smuggling boat heading west with narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a drug bust at sea; in fact the boat is the definition and seize is the word that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a barge is a flat-bottomed cargo vessel used on canals and rivers.

clue.text: Life force found within Pinocchio (3)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the name

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of the puppet's name, after PINO

explanation.surface: The spark that makes a wooden puppet come alive.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinocchio is the puppet who came to life, so the life force fits the story too.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi (qi) is the vital energy of Chinese philosophy.

clue.text: Compare story-telling with cartoon bear leading and jumping cross-legged (5,6)

indicators.note: 'with' means together with, so the compare and story-telling pieces are joined side by side
whoever is leading walks in front, so the bear goes at the start of the answer

blocks.note: Yogi Bear of the Hanna-Barbera cartoons
cf. is the abbreviation for compare

explanation.surface: A children's storyteller compares tales with a cartoon bear who hops about in a lotus pose.
explanation.walkthrough: Story-telling is the childish euphemism for fibbing. Yogic flying is the Transcendental Meditation practice of hopping while seated cross-legged.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogic flying is hopping along while sitting in the lotus position.

clue.text: Combine core part of chimney and old fireplace (6)

indicators.note: the core of anything is its centre, so take the letter at the very middle of the word

blocks.note: M is the central letter of chiMney
an ingle is an old word for a hearth, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: Building instructions: join the middle of the chimney stack to an antique hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: Combine is a verb here, matching mingle.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to mix things together.

clue.text: Laid songs out in series of notes (9)

indicators.note: the letters are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A composer sets out their songs as a run of musical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface keeps you thinking of scores; the answer is itself a musical term, a slide through a run of notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a rapid slide up or down through a series of notes.

clue.text: Hunter — one regularly taking fewer traps (7)

indicators.note: LESS holds I and ON inside it

blocks.note: on a medicine is regularly taking it

explanation.surface: A hunter who sets fewer traps than before.
explanation.walkthrough: Regularly taking looks like an alternate-letters instruction, but it means ON, as in on statins. It is the lioness, not the lion, who does most of a pride's hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionesses do most of the hunting for a pride.

clue.text: Something that reveals palpebral muscle? (3-6)

blocks.note: a surprising discovery that shows you something you had not seen
palpebral means of the eyelid; the muscle literally opens the eye

explanation.surface: An anatomy question about what shows the eyelid muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: Palpebral is an obscure word for 'of the eyelid'; the muscle that lifts the lid is literally an eye opener.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a surprising revelation, and a muscle that raises the eyelid opens the eye.

clue.text: Lift across the pond to reveal rocks (8)

indicators.note: the letters are rocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An American lift opens to show a pile of stones.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocks is a noun in the surface but a verb here. Across the pond means in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: what Britons call a lift, Americans (across the Atlantic) call by this name.

clue.text: Set fire to gas when there’s no energy left for element (7)

indicators.note: remove E (energy) and L (left)

blocks.clueFragment: gas when there’s no energy left
blocks.note: HELIUM, a gas, without E and L

explanation.surface: A chemist ignites a gas once its energy has run out, to obtain an element.
explanation.walkthrough: No energy left sounds like exhaustion; it removes two letters, E for energy and L for left.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithium is a chemical element, the lightest metal.

clue.text: Someone going through penance more quickly (6)

blocks.note: one who fasts, as in Lent

explanation.surface: A penitent hurrying through their penance.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced the same but come from different roots: going without food, and speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A faster abstains from food as penance; faster also means more quickly.

clue.text: Pretence regularly cloaked by quiet delivery (6)

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so take letters at a steady every-other spacing
SH wraps around the letters

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken way of talking that masks a pretence.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivery means a way of speaking here, not a parcel arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker's delivery is their speech, the way they talk.

clue.text: Five nudes jumping over tree backwards — it’s a work of art (5,2,4)

indicators.note: the letters of NUDES leap about
O and LIME are read in reverse

explanation.surface: Five naked figures leap backwards over a tree, which sounds like a sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: O and LIME make OLIME, which reverses to EMILO. The nudes fit the famous armless statue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venus de Milo is the ancient Greek marble statue in the Louvre.

clue.text: Group performing without safety device? (5)

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside: NET goes around ON

explanation.surface: Trapeze artists perform without a safety net.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface splits the answer as 'no net', which is exactly the trap: 'without' here is the old sense of outside, as in the hymn line 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this is a group of nine performers, or a piece written for them.

clue.text: Bad egg turning green (5)

indicators.note: EVIL and O are turned round together

explanation.surface: A rotten egg going green.
explanation.walkthrough: Bad egg is a set phrase for a rogue, which hides the split between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a dull yellowish-green colour.

clue.text: Love intervening for and on behalf of father (3)

indicators.note: O comes between the two P's

blocks.note: pp = per procurationem, written when signing for someone else

explanation.surface: Love steps in to speak up for Dad.
explanation.walkthrough: pp is what you write before signing a letter on someone else's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal, chiefly American word for a dad.

clue.text: Muscle connector lacks density for part of joint (5)

indicators.note: a thing that lacks something does not have it, so the letter for density is removed

blocks.note: a tendon joins muscle to bone

explanation.surface: An anatomy note: a tendon missing its density, in part of a knee.
explanation.walkthrough: The anatomy surface makes you think of a body joint; the answer is a carpentry joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting tongue that fits into a mortise to make a joint.

clue.text: Honour the German church incorporating new submissiveness (9)

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take into the body of something, so 'the German church' takes the new letter into itself

blocks.note: OBE = Officer of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: Honouring a German church that has brought in a new meekness.
explanation.walkthrough: The German looks like a nationality; it asks for the German word for 'the'. DIE and CE together take N in at their join.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name a willingness to do as one is told.

clue.text: Revised name or term accommodating latest in technology? (8)

definitions.text: Revised name or term accommodating latest in technology?

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so the letters of name or term are put in a new order
to accommodate a guest is to give them room, so the reworked letters make room for one more
the latest in a sequence is the one at the end, so take the final letter

explanation.surface: A dictionary definition of a new name forced on an old thing by modern tech.
explanation.walkthrough: N for name is a dictionary abbreviation. The whole clue is also the definition: a retronym renames something because technology moved on, as with 'acoustic guitar'.
explanation.definitionFit: A retronym is a new name for an old thing, coined after a newer version appeared.

clue.text: Go through curved opening at 135 degrees (6)

blocks.note: on a compass, 135 degrees is south-east
an arch is a curved opening

explanation.surface: Walk through a rounded doorway set at an angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 135 degrees looks like geometry; it is a compass bearing, south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: going through someone's pockets means hunting through them.
